_comment: Rules for inferring bike MODEL and TRIM from an item's description text.
Edit this file and re-run `npm run classify` — no code changes needed.
Why description-first: the Lightspeed category tree is maintained by hand, so it
has gaps (79% of BIKE items carry no trim node) and errors (the tree literally
contains the typo 'EPXERT'). An item's own description is entered per-product and
has proven more complete. The category tree is still used for the model vocabulary
and as a cross-check — see /api/model-audit for disagreements.
extraModels: models seen in descriptions but absent from the category tree
modelAliases: abbreviations used in descriptions -> canonical model name.
trims: canonical trim levels, matched longest-first. Aliases map to the canonical.
kinds: keyword -> item kind. A frameset, frame, build kit or rental is NOT a
complete bike; lumping them together overstates model sales badly (a frameset
and a complete bike differ by tens of thousands of rand).
_sizeComment: Frame size is read from the END of the description ('EPIC 8 SW CARB/BLUPRL L').
sizeAliases normalise spelling variants. wheelTokens are diameters, NOT frame
sizes — a description ending '29' or '27.5' names the wheel and carries no
size, so treating it as one would invent a size that does not exist.
Each size gets a SYSTEM: alpha (S/M/L), s-sizing (S1-S6, Specialized MTB),
